provenance.note: Cost and time are the REAL figures from the live calls that produced these findings. Re-running from demo/live_run/cache/ replays them for $0.00 — that is a replay, not a fresh measurement.

runtime.note: Wall clock is recorded per INVOCATION, and this file was last written by a cache replay, so a single top-level number would be misleading. The figures below name what each measures. Analytical outputs are unaffected: no finding, candidate or cost value is derived from any of these.
runtime.analysis_definition: Sum of the measured wall clock of the two invocations that made live model calls. Includes one superseded set of reasoning calls (run 1's stages 3-4) that were discarded and re-run after a Stage 2 fix, so this is the total cost in time of producing these findings, not the minimum achievable.

producing_runs.produced: Stage 1 extractions for all 2,398 work orders (2,388 live calls)
producing_runs.superseded: Its stages 3-4 ran against a 57-candidate set and were discarded when the serial-cohort grouping and examine-depth were fixed.

producing_runs.produced: Stages 3-4 for all 31 examined candidates (64 live calls). Stage 1 replayed from cache at zero cost.

runtime.last_invocation_kind: cache replay — every stage served from demo/live_run/cache/, no model calls, $0.00. Not a measurement of the analysis.
runtime.stage_seconds_note: accounting.stages[*].seconds is summed across concurrent workers, not elapsed. At 16-way concurrency it over-states elapsed time by roughly 16x and must not be presented as run time.
runtime.reconstruction: The committed manifest never held the correct value: git shows a single commit (27e37cf) for this file, already carrying the replay's 0.4s. The two run totals are recovered from the runs' own stdout, archived under provenance/. They corroborate against this manifest's per-stage cost and token counts, which match the logs exactly.
